findings.title: AssignmentSource queued datetime is placed in Celery task kwargs
findings.body: assignment_source.to_dict() returns the raw datetime object for `queued` (dataclasses.asdict does not convert it), and that dict is passed directly as a sync_assignee_outbound Celery kwarg. Sentry tasks use serializable primitive kwargs, so in production this either fails to enqueue/serialize or is degraded to a string by the JSON encoder, unlike the eager self.tasks() test path which can pass the object through in-process. The new inbound-to-outbound path can therefore error or lose the intended type exactly when an external webhook triggers an assignment.

findings.title: queued default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the dataclass class is defined, not when each AssignmentSource is created. Every source created by a long-lived worker/web process will share the process-import timestamp instead of its actual queue time. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now) so each assignment source records when it was created.

findings.title: from_dict does not restore or validate the queued/integration fields after serialization
findings.body: from_dict blindly does cls(**input_dict). If `queued` has been serialized to an ISO string for transport, it is stored back as a str despite the declared datetime type; similarly integration_id is not coerced/validated. Any current or future logic that compares, formats, or expires based on `queued`, or compares integration_id as an int, can then behave incorrectly or raise, while the tests only cover dicts that omit `queued` entirely.

findings.title: No test proves a different integration still receives outbound sync, or that deassign is blocked for the source
findings.body: The new matching-source test only covers assign with a single linked integration and asserts that integration is not called. It does not cover the stated intended behavior that other integrations still propagate the change, nor the deassign/unassign path with a matching assignment_source. A regression that blocks all outbound syncs for any non-None source, compares the wrong integration id, or only fixes assign would pass the added tests while breaking cross-integration sync or leaving the unassign cycle intact.
